units.name: cli-flags
units.description: This is the part of ripgrep that understands the command line. It reads the raw words typed after `rg` (plus anything from a config file pointed to by the RIPGREP_CONFIG_PATH environment variable), figures out which flags, search patterns, and file paths the user meant, checks that the combination makes sense, and turns it all into one clean, structured bundle of settings that the rest of the program can simply read from. It also knows how to write out the help text, the man page, and shell tab-completion scripts, since those are just different descriptions of the same set of flags. It must never itself search files, read matches, or print search results — its job ends at producing (or describing) the user's request, not fulfilling it.
units.role: Parses argv + config file into a validated, high-level arguments structure, and generates help/man/completion text describing that same flag surface.

entrypoints.name: flags::parse

entrypoints.name: HiArgs

Exposes dozens of accessor methods (mode, threads, matcher, searcher, haystack_builder, walk_builder, stdout, types, index_read/index_write, stats, sort, quit_after_match, ...) that main.rs and the index integration read to drive the actual work.

units.name: rg-orchestrator
units.description: This is the brain of the `rg` command: the code that runs once the command-line options have already been understood, and decides what ripgrep actually does. It builds the list of files and directories to look through, hands each one to the search engine, prints results (or file names, or statistics) to the screen, and figures out what exit code the program should return (0 = found something, 1 = found nothing, 2 = an error happened). It also owns small shared plumbing that both the option-parsing code and the search code need: a simple logger that prints diagnostic messages to the terminal, and a tiny 'did an error happen / should we print messages' status board. It must never silently swallow real errors, must handle a broken output pipe gracefully instead of crashing, and must not itself parse command-line flags or implement the low-level text-matching algorithm.
units.role: Top-level control flow that wires together CLI arguments, directory walking, file searching, and result printing into the running `rg` process.

entrypoints.name: main
entrypoints.plain: The OS process entry point for the rg binary; invoked when the user runs `rg`.

entrypoints.name: Logger::init
entrypoints.plain: Turns on ripgrep's stderr logger; called by the flag-parsing code as soon as it starts.

entrypoints.name: messages::set_messages

entrypoints.name: messages::set_ignore_messages

entrypoints.name: Printer

Spawns an external preprocessor command to transform file contents before searching (search.rs:303-306).

Initializes the global `log` logger singleton (logger.rs:16-27) and maintains global atomic flags for whether messages are enabled and whether an error occurred (messages.rs:18-25), read/written from multiple threads during parallel search.

units.name: grep-facade
units.description: This is a tiny organizational wrapper, not a feature. The `grep` crate published to crates.io bundles six separate ripgrep library crates (grep-cli, grep-matcher, grep-pcre2, grep-printer, grep-regex, grep-searcher) behind a single dependency so that outside consumers only need to add one line to their project instead of six. It does nothing but re-export each crate under a short module name; it contains no logic, no data structures, and no behavior of its own, and it must never grow any.
units.role: Single-dependency re-export bundle exposing the six grep-* library crates as one crate.

entrypoints.name: cli
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the grep_cli crate as module `cli`.

entrypoints.name: matcher
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the grep_matcher crate as module `matcher`.

entrypoints.name: pcre2
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the grep_pcre2 crate as module `pcre2` (only when the `pcre2` feature is enabled).

entrypoints.name: printer
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the grep_printer crate as module `printer`.

entrypoints.name: regex
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the grep_regex crate as module `regex`.

entrypoints.name: searcher
entrypoints.plain: Re-exports the grep_searcher crate as module `searcher`.

units.name: grep-matcher
units.description: This unit defines the common rulebook that all of ripgrep's different pattern-matching engines must follow. Instead of every part of ripgrep needing to know the details of the Rust regex engine versus the PCRE2 engine, they all just need to understand this one shared vocabulary: what a 'match' looks like, how to report captured groups, what counts as the end of a line, and how to substitute matched text back into a replacement string (for --replace). It contains no actual searching logic itself — it is purely the shared contract that lets ripgrep swap search engines in and out without the rest of the program noticing the difference.
units.role: Defines the Matcher/Captures trait interface and supporting types that all regex-engine crates implement and all consumer crates program against.

entrypoints.name: Matcher
entrypoints.plain: The core trait every regex/pattern engine implements, and that search/print code depends on to run searches without caring which engine is underneath.

entrypoints.name: Match
entrypoints.plain: A simple 'this text from here to here matched' value, used everywhere a match position needs to be passed around.

entrypoints.name: Captures
entrypoints.plain: The interface each engine's capture-group results must implement, so callers can fetch capture group N without knowing the engine-specific representation.

entrypoints.name: Captures::interpolate
entrypoints.plain: Expands $1/${name} references in a user-supplied replacement string using the actual matched capture text; used to implement --replace.

entrypoints.name: NoCaptures
entrypoints.plain: A ready-made 'no capture groups supported' implementation.

entrypoints.name: NoError
entrypoints.plain: A ready-made 'this matcher can never fail' error type.

entrypoints.name: LineTerminator
entrypoints.plain: Represents what counts as 'end of a line', shared across the search pipeline.

entrypoints.name: ByteSet
entrypoints.plain: A set of bytes guaranteed to never appear in a match; used for search optimization hints.

entrypoints.name: LineMatchKind
entrypoints.plain: Describes whether a fast line-scan found a confirmed match or just a candidate needing verification.

units.name: grep-regex
units.description: This is ripgrep's default 'brain' for understanding search patterns. Given the text pattern the user typed plus options like ignore-case, whole-word, multi-line, or literal text, it parses the pattern, figures out the best way to search for it quickly, and produces a ready-to-use matcher object. That matcher is what the rest of ripgrep calls, over and over, to find where the pattern occurs in each file's text.
units.role: Compiles rg's pattern syntax and search options into a fast Matcher implementation backed by Rust's regex-automata/regex-syntax engines.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcherBuilder
entrypoints.plain: The configuration object callers fill in (case sensitivity, multiline, word boundary, fixed strings, line terminator, etc.) before building a matcher.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcherBuilder::new
entrypoints.plain: Starts a fresh, default configuration for building a matcher; used from cli-flags.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcherBuilder::build
entrypoints.plain: Turns one pattern string plus the configured options into a working matcher.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcherBuilder::build_many
entrypoints.plain: Same as build, but for multiple patterns joined as an OR.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcher
entrypoints.plain: The compiled matcher object the searcher drives to find matches in text.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcher::new
entrypoints.plain: Convenience constructor for a matcher with default options.

entrypoints.name: RegexCaptures
entrypoints.plain: Holds capture-group positions for a single match; implements grep-matcher's Captures.

entrypoints.name: Error
entrypoints.plain: The error type returned when a pattern can't be compiled, surfaced to the CLI layer.

units.name: grep-pcre2
units.description: This piece of ripgrep lets the program hand off searching to PCRE2, a well-known external pattern-matching library, whenever a user asks for advanced pattern features (backreferences, lookaround) that ripgrep's own built-in search engine cannot handle. It configures and compiles patterns using PCRE2, then wraps the result so the rest of ripgrep can use it exactly like any other search engine, without needing to know PCRE2 is involved.
units.role: Adapts the external PCRE2 pattern-matching library to ripgrep's internal Matcher interface, used only when the user opts in with -P/--pcre2.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcherBuilder
entrypoints.plain: The configuration object for setting up PCRE2 options (case sensitivity, word boundaries, JIT, Unicode mode, etc.).

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcherBuilder::new
entrypoints.plain: Creates a default builder; called from cli-flags.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcherBuilder::build
entrypoints.plain: Compiles a pattern string into a usable PCRE2 matcher.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcherBuilder::build_many
entrypoints.plain: Compiles multiple patterns into a single combined matcher.

entrypoints.name: RegexMatcher
entrypoints.plain: The compiled PCRE2 matcher object, used by ripgrep's search dispatch.

entrypoints.name: version
entrypoints.plain: Reports the linked PCRE2 library's version, used in --version output.

entrypoints.name: is_jit_available
entrypoints.plain: Reports whether PCRE2's JIT is available, used in --version output.

entrypoints.name: Error
entrypoints.plain: The error type returned when a PCRE2 pattern can't be compiled.

units.name: grep-searcher
units.description: This is the engine that actually reads through a file or stream of text and finds the parts that match a search pattern. Given a matcher and a source of bytes (an open file, a memory-mapped file, or any readable stream), it reads the data efficiently, converts it from other text encodings when needed, detects and skips binary data, splits the data into lines, keeps track of surrounding context lines around each match, and counts line numbers. For every match or context line it finds, it hands the result to a plug-in ('Sink') supplied by the caller, which decides what to do with it.
units.role: Core line-oriented search engine: turns a byte source plus a pattern matcher into a stream of match/context events delivered to a caller-supplied Sink.

entrypoints.name: Searcher
entrypoints.plain: The main object that runs a search; created via SearcherBuilder and reused across searches.

entrypoints.name: SearcherBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures search options (context lines, binary detection, encoding, memory-map policy) before building a Searcher.

entrypoints.name: Searcher::search_path
entrypoints.plain: Opens a file by path and searches it, choosing memory-map or buffered reading automatically.

entrypoints.name: Searcher::search_file
entrypoints.plain: Searches an already-open file handle.

entrypoints.name: Searcher::search_reader
entrypoints.plain: Searches any generic readable stream, such as stdin.

entrypoints.name: Searcher::search_slice
entrypoints.plain: Searches an in-memory byte slice directly.

entrypoints.name: Sink
entrypoints.plain: The callback interface a caller must implement to receive search results (matches, context lines, binary-data notices, begin/finish events). Implemented by grep-printer's Standard/Json/Summary printers.

entrypoints.name: SinkMatch
entrypoints.plain: The data describing a single match, passed to Sink::matched.

entrypoints.name: SinkContext
entrypoints.plain: The data describing a contextual (before/after) line, passed to Sink::context.

entrypoints.name: SinkFinish
entrypoints.plain: Summary data (bytes searched, binary offset) passed to Sink::finish.

entrypoints.name: MmapChoice
entrypoints.plain: Lets a caller opt in to memory-map based reading.

entrypoints.name: BinaryDetection
entrypoints.plain: Configures how binary (non-text) data is detected and handled.

entrypoints.name: LineIter
entrypoints.plain: Line-splitting iterator available for callers to iterate lines within a SinkMatch/SinkContext.

effects.description: Opens a file by path (searcher/mod.rs:655), reads file size via metadata (mod.rs:963), and creates a memory map of an open file via memmap::Mmap::map with a sequential-access hint on Unix (mmap.rs:84-89).

Generic buffered reading from any io::Read source, including stdin, via the internal line buffer (line_buffer.rs:418, mod.rs:965,990); also transcodes non-UTF-8 input (BOM sniffing, UTF-16) via encoding_rs (mod.rs:322-328,741-744).

units.name: grep-printer
units.description: This is the part of ripgrep that takes the raw list of matches found in a file and turns them into something a person or another program can actually read. Depending on the requested output style, it can produce the familiar colored terminal listing with line numbers and highlighted matches, a stream of JSON records for scripts, a plain summary such as a match count, or a bare list of file paths (optionally clickable via terminal hyperlinks). It also keeps running totals such as how many files, lines, and matches were seen and how long the search took, for reporting with --stats. It never opens files or a terminal itself; it is always handed an existing output destination to write into.
units.role: Formats search results found by the search engine into ripgrep's various output formats: standard colored text, JSON Lines, and summary/count output.

entrypoints.name: StandardBuilder::build
entrypoints.plain: Configures and creates a printer that produces the classic colored/terminal search-result listing.

entrypoints.name: Standard::sink_with_path
entrypoints.plain: Produces the per-file adapter that the searcher feeds matches into, associated with a given file path.

entrypoints.name: JSONBuilder::build
entrypoints.plain: Creates a printer that emits one JSON object per line of output, for --json.

entrypoints.name: JSON::sink_with_path
entrypoints.plain: Produces the per-file adapter for JSON output.

entrypoints.name: SummaryBuilder::build
entrypoints.plain: Creates a printer that reports aggregate results rather than every individual match line, for -c/--count and --files-with-matches.

entrypoints.name: Summary::sink_with_path
entrypoints.plain: Produces the per-file adapter for summary output.

entrypoints.name: Sink::stats
entrypoints.plain: Lets the caller retrieve the running statistics (bytes/lines/matches searched, elapsed time) after a search, for --stats. Implemented identically by StandardSink, SummarySink, and JSONSink.

entrypoints.name: ColorSpecs::new

entrypoints.name: HyperlinkConfig::new

effects.description: Reads the system clock to time each search for --stats reporting via std::time::Instant (standard.rs:529,843; json.rs:513,804; summary.rs:406,704).

units.name: ignore
units.description: This is the component that decides which files and folders a search should actually look at. As ripgrep walks through a directory tree, this unit checks each file and folder against the same kind of rules that Git uses (.gitignore files, .git/info/exclude, global git ignore settings) plus ripgrep's own .ignore/.rgignore files, hidden-file rules, user-specified include/exclude patterns, and file-type filters. It also does the actual directory traversal itself, either one file at a time or in parallel across multiple threads, so that irrelevant content like build output or explicitly excluded files never gets opened or searched.
units.role: Recursively walks the filesystem (serially or in parallel) while applying gitignore-style, override, and file-type rules to decide which paths to yield to the caller.

entrypoints.name: WalkBuilder
entrypoints.plain: The configuration object used to say 'walk this directory, respecting .gitignore etc., with these options', then turned into an actual iterator.

entrypoints.name: Walk
entrypoints.plain: A single-threaded iterator that yields one file/directory at a time, already filtered by ignore rules.

entrypoints.name: WalkParallel
entrypoints.plain: The multi-threaded version of the walker; the caller supplies a callback/visitor invoked once per file/directory found.

entrypoints.name: WalkState
entrypoints.plain: The signal a caller's per-entry callback returns to tell the parallel walker whether to keep going, skip a directory, or stop.

entrypoints.name: DirEntry
entrypoints.plain: One file or directory result yielded by the walker, along with any error encountered reading its ignore files.

entrypoints.name: ParallelVisitor
entrypoints.plain: The interface a caller implements to receive entries from the parallel walker on each worker thread (ParallelVisitor/ParallelVisitorBuilder).

entrypoints.name: Override
entrypoints.plain: Lets a caller explicitly force-include or force-exclude paths by glob pattern (e.g. -g/--glob), overriding the normal ignore-file rules.

entrypoints.name: Types
entrypoints.plain: Lets a caller filter by file type using a built-in and user-extensible catalog of file-type glob definitions.

entrypoints.name: IncrementalIgnore
entrypoints.plain: A lazily-loading, cacheable ignore-rule checker for a single path, letting a caller test individual paths against gitignore-style rules without a full directory walk.

effects.description: Recursively reads directory trees (via walkdir for the serial Walk, or raw std::fs::read_dir for WalkParallel, walk.rs:605,1617); opens and parses ignore files line-by-line (gitignore.rs:407-412); locates a repo's .git directory (dir.rs:1070,1088); reads git config files to resolve core.excludesFile (gitignore.rs:611-646); reads file metadata/device numbers for symlink and same-file-system handling (walk.rs:2171-2186).

Reads GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL, GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, and HOME to locate global gitignore/config files (gitignore.rs:607-703), and calls current_dir() to resolve relative paths and global gitignore patterns (walk.rs:1082, gitignore.rs:142).
Spawns OS threads for the parallel walker using a work-stealing deque (walk.rs:1526).

units.name: globset
units.description: This is the part of ripgrep that understands glob patterns the way a shell does - things like '*.rs', '**/target/', or 'src/{foo,bar}.rs'. Given such a pattern, it can quickly check whether a given file path matches it, and it can also check a whole batch of patterns against one path at once, reporting back exactly which ones matched. It only deals with pattern text and path strings; it has no idea what gitignore rules are, what command-line flags exist, or how to walk a directory tree - those are handled by other parts of the program that build on top of this one.
units.role: Compiles shell-style glob patterns into fast matchers and matches sets of globs against candidate paths.

entrypoints.name: Glob::new
entrypoints.plain: Parses a single glob pattern string into a reusable Glob value.

entrypoints.name: Glob::compile_matcher
entrypoints.plain: Turns a parsed Glob into a ready-to-use single-pattern matcher.

entrypoints.name: GlobBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Lets a caller configure matching behavior (case sensitivity, whether '*' crosses '/', backslash escaping) before compiling a glob.

entrypoints.name: GlobMatcher::is_match
entrypoints.plain: Checks whether one compiled glob matches a given path.

entrypoints.name: GlobSet
entrypoints.plain: Represents a compiled group of glob patterns.

entrypoints.name: GlobSet::is_match
entrypoints.plain: Checks a path against every glob in the set at once.

entrypoints.name: GlobSetBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Incrementally collects individual Glob patterns and compiles them into one GlobSet.

entrypoints.name: Candidate::new
entrypoints.plain: Precomputes/normalizes a path once so it can be matched against many globs cheaply.

entrypoints.name: Error
entrypoints.plain: The error type returned when a glob pattern fails to parse or compile.

units.name: grep-cli
units.description: This is a toolbox of small, operating-system-facing helpers that any command-line search program needs but that have nothing to do with search logic itself. It answers questions like: is the program's input coming from a keyboard/terminal or being piped in? Should output be colored and how should it be buffered? If a file is compressed, how do you transparently unpack it by handing it off to an external decompression program? How do you display text that might contain broken or unusual bytes safely? Plus small utilities like reading the machine's hostname and turning a human-friendly size like '2M' into a byte count. None of this code knows anything about regular expressions or matching text.
units.role: Provides OS/terminal-facing plumbing (tty detection, colored/buffered stdout, external decompression via subprocesses, byte-safe escaping, hostname lookup, human-readable size parsing) used by ripgrep's command-line front end.

entrypoints.name: is_readable_stdin

entrypoints.name: StandardStream

entrypoints.name: stdout

entrypoints.name: stdout_buffered_block

entrypoints.name: patterns_from_stdin
entrypoints.plain: Reads patterns from stdin when '-f -' is used.

entrypoints.name: pattern_from_os

entrypoints.name: resolve_binary

entrypoints.name: CommandReader::new
entrypoints.plain: Streams stdout from a child process (e.g. a user-supplied --pre preprocessor) while capturing stderr for good error messages.

entrypoints.name: hostname
entrypoints.plain: Returns the machine's hostname, used e.g. for hyperlink generation.

entrypoints.name: parse_human_readable_size
entrypoints.plain: Parses flag values like '2M' or '10G' into byte counts, for --max-filesize.

entrypoints.name: DecompressionReaderBuilder
entrypoints.plain: Configures transparent decompression of .gz/.xz/.bz2/etc. files by spawning the matching decompressor program.

entrypoints.name: DecompressionReader
entrypoints.plain: The reader that streams decompressed file contents, or passes the file through unchanged if no matching tool is found; used for -z/--search-zip.

effects.description: Spawns external decompression programs (gzip, bzip2, xz, lz4, brotli, zstd, uncompress) as child processes (decompress.rs:182,490-532), and provides generic child-process spawning/streaming/reaping for arbitrary commands with piped stdout/stderr (process.rs:104-118,218-252).
Reads the PATH environment variable to resolve executables before invoking them (decompress.rs:462,469).
Checks whether resolved candidate binaries exist via metadata (decompress.rs:453-455); opens the raw file for passthrough (non-decompressed) reads (decompress.rs:362).

Retrieves the machine hostname via direct libc gethostname/sysconf calls on Unix, or the Windows computer-name API (hostname.rs:20,41,60).
Reads directly from process stdin to parse patterns piped into the program (pattern.rs:105-106).

units.name: grep-index
units.description: This is an experimental, opt-in feature that lets ripgrep remember what it has already learned about the files in a directory, so future searches over the same directory can go faster. It works by breaking file contents into small overlapping chunks of text and saving, in a small database file on disk, which chunks appear in which files. When a later search comes in, it can first check this saved index to figure out which files could not possibly contain the search term, and skip reading those files entirely. The feature is marked experimental and must be explicitly turned on.
units.role: Builds, opens, and locates a small on-disk n-gram index of file contents so ripgrep can skip files that provably don't match a search.

entrypoints.name: IndexDiscovery::new

entrypoints.name: IndexDiscovery::create

entrypoints.name: IndexDiscovery::discover
entrypoints.plain: Walks up from the current directory (or an env-var override) to find an existing index, or creates one, and opens the database inside it.

entrypoints.name: Index::builder

entrypoints.name: Index::exists

entrypoints.name: Index::path
entrypoints.plain: Returns the on-disk location of the opened index's database file.

entrypoints.name: GramQueryBuilder::build
entrypoints.plain: Turns a compiled regular expression into a boolean query over n-grams that could be evaluated against the on-disk index to rule out files.

effects.description: Creates/opens an embedded redb database file to persist the index (index.rs:62,73,80), and runs read transactions against it (index.rs:181-189).
Creates the index directory (index.rs:53) and checks for the index file/directory's existence (index.rs:22-25).

Reads the RIPGREP_INDEX_PATH environment variable to override the index location (index.rs:132), and reads the current working directory as the starting point for locating a '.ripgrep' index (index.rs:124).

violations_observed.note: cli-flags imports and constructs rg-orchestrator's own types (HaystackBuilder from haystack.rs; SearchWorkerBuilder/PatternMatcher/Printer from search.rs) directly by module path, and cli-flags/parse.rs calls rg-orchestrator's Logger::init and messages::set_messages/set_ignore_messages. This makes the two units mutually dependent rather than a clean one-directional 'orchestrator drives leaf units' relationship: rg-orchestrator drives cli-flags (calls flags::parse, reads HiArgs), while cli-flags simultaneously builds and returns rg-orchestrator's own domain types. Both directions target entrypoints that are explicitly declared on the receiving unit, so no undeclared-symbol invariant is broken, but the two units are architecturally entangled and might be better modeled as one unit or split along a different seam in a future pass.
